newsitem.title: USA: NYC council may ask halt to Swiss bank investing.
newsitem.headline: NYC council may ask halt to Swiss bank investing.

text.p: The New York City Council on Thursday, saying it will go ahead with hearings on how Swiss banks treated Holocaust victims, added it would ask city firms to stop investing with the banks if the issue were not solved.
Jewish leaders on Thursday dropped plans to consider mounting a world-wide boycott of Swiss banks after the banks established a Holocaust memorial fund, a World Jewish Congress offical said.

However, New York City Council Speaker Peter Vallone, while praising the Swiss banks for agreeing to set-up a $70 million humanitarian fund, said it was still important to hold the hearings to inform the public.

And in a prepared statement, he "cautioned that if the Swiss banks did not continue on the path to fulfilling their financial commitments, he would ask New York City's business community to voluntarily decline to invest with those institutions until restitution has been made."

The city council has drafted a bill that would stop the city from depositing or investing city funds in Swiss banks until "adequate restitution" is made to victims of the Holocaust. The reputations of Swiss banks have been tarnished by allegations they kept millions of dollars that were owned by Holocaust victims.
